subject: Biology
title: Animal Kingdom
summary: Animals are classified on basic features: level of organisation, symmetry, germ layers, coelom, segmentation and notochord.

Non-chordates run from Porifera (cellular level) and Cnidaria (tissue level, radial, diploblastic) through flatworms, roundworms and annelids to arthropods (the largest phylum), molluscs, echinoderms and hemichordates.
Chordates have a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits at some stage. Vertebrates replace the notochord with a vertebral column.
Vertebrate classes — cyclostomes, cartilaginous and bony fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals — differ in skin, heart, respiration, temperature regulation and reproduction.

formulas.name: Levels of organisation
formulas.formula: cellular (Porifera) → tissue (Cnidaria, Ctenophora) → organ (Platyhelminthes) → organ system (Aschelminthes onwards)

formulas.name: Symmetry
formulas.formula: asymmetrical (most sponges);  radial (Cnidaria, Ctenophora, adult Echinodermata);  bilateral (Platyhelminthes onwards)
formulas.note: Echinoderm larvae are bilateral; adults are radial.

formulas.name: Germ layers
formulas.formula: diploblastic: ectoderm + endoderm with mesoglea (Cnidaria, Ctenophora);  triploblastic: + mesoderm (Platyhelminthes to Chordata)

formulas.name: Coelom
formulas.formula: acoelomate: Platyhelminthes;  pseudocoelomate: Aschelminthes;  coelomate: Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Hemichordata, Chordata

formulas.name: Porifera
formulas.formula: canal system (ostia → spongocoel → osculum), choanocytes (collar cells), spicules/spongin fibres; hermaphrodite; internal fertilisation; indirect development

formulas.name: Cnidaria and Ctenophora
formulas.formula: Cnidaria: cnidoblasts (stinging cells), polyp and medusa forms, metagenesis (Obelia) — Hydra, Physalia, Adamsia, Pennatula, Meandrina;  Ctenophora: comb plates, bioluminescence — Pleurobrachia, Ctenoplana

formulas.name: Worms
formulas.formula: Platyhelminthes: flattened, flame cells, hooks/suckers (Taenia, Fasciola, Planaria regenerates);  Aschelminthes: round, separate sexes, female larger (Ascaris, Wuchereria, Ancylostoma);  Annelida: metameric segmentation, nephridia, closed circulation (Nereis, Pheretima, Hirudinaria)

formulas.name: Arthropoda
formulas.formula: jointed appendages, chitinous exoskeleton, open circulation; respiration by gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheae; Malpighian tubules; compound eyes, statocysts
formulas.when: Largest phylum (over two-thirds of animal species).

formulas.name: Mollusca and Echinodermata
formulas.formula: Mollusca: soft body, mantle, calcareous shell, radula, ctenidia (Pila, Pinctada, Sepia, Loligo, Octopus);  Echinodermata: spiny calcareous ossicles, water vascular system (tube feet), all marine (Asterias, Echinus, Antedon, Cucumaria, Ophiura)
formulas.mistake: Sepia (cuttlefish), Loligo (squid) and Octopus (devil fish) are molluscs, not fish.

formulas.name: Chordate features
formulas.formula: notochord + dorsal hollow nerve cord + paired pharyngeal gill slits + post-anal tail

formulas.name: Chordate subphyla
formulas.formula: Urochordata: notochord only in larval tail (Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum);  Cephalochordata: notochord from head to tail throughout life (Branchiostoma/Amphioxus);  Vertebrata: vertebral column

formulas.name: Heart chambers
formulas.formula: fish 2;  amphibians and reptiles 3 (crocodile 4);  birds and mammals 4

formulas.name: Vertebrate classes
formulas.formula: Cyclostomata (jawless, suctorial mouth — Petromyzon, Myxine);  Chondrichthyes (cartilage, placoid scales, no air bladder — Scoliodon, Pristis, Trygon, Torpedo);  Osteichthyes (bone, operculum, air bladder — Labeo, Catla, Hippocampus, Exocoetus);  Amphibia (moist skin, cloaca — Rana, Bufo, Salamandra, Ichthyophis);  Reptilia (dry scaly skin — Chelone, Chameleon, Naja, Vipera);  Aves (feathers, pneumatic bones — Corvus, Columba, Struthio, Pavo);  Mammalia (hair, mammary glands, external ears — Ornithorhynchus oviparous, Macropus, Pteropus, Balaenoptera)

formulas.name: Cold vs warm blooded
formulas.formula: poikilothermous: fish, amphibians, reptiles;  homoiothermous: birds and mammals

examples.title: Metagenesis
examples.problem: What is metagenesis? Give an example.
examples.solution: Alternation of polyp (asexual) and medusa (sexual) generations in some cnidarians — Obelia: polyps produce medusae asexually; medusae form polyps sexually.

examples.title: Pseudocoelom
examples.problem: Which phylum has a pseudocoelom, and what does that mean?
examples.solution: Aschelminthes (roundworms). The body cavity is not lined fully by mesoderm; mesoderm appears as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm.

examples.title: Not a fish
examples.problem: Which of these is a true fish: jellyfish, starfish, cuttlefish, flying fish, silverfish?
examples.solution: Only the flying fish (Exocoetus, Osteichthyes). Jellyfish — Cnidaria; starfish — Echinodermata; cuttlefish — Mollusca; silverfish — insect (Arthropoda).

examples.title: Electric organ and poison sting
examples.problem: Which cartilaginous fish has an electric organ and which has a poison sting?
examples.solution: Torpedo has electric organs; Trygon (sting ray) has a poison sting.

examples.title: Excretory structures
examples.problem: Match: flame cells, nephridia, Malpighian tubules, green glands.
examples.solution: Flame cells — Platyhelminthes; nephridia — Annelida; Malpighian tubules — most insects (Arthropoda); green glands — crustaceans like prawn.

topics.title: Segmentation
topics.explain: Metameric segmentation — the body is divided externally and internally into repeated segments with serial repetition of some organs — appears in Annelida (earthworm), Arthropoda and Chordata.

topics.title: Hemichordata
topics.explain: Worm-like marine animals with a proboscis, collar and trunk; earlier placed under Chordata but they have a stomochord (not a true notochord) and are now a separate non-chordate phylum: Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus.

topics.title: Arthropod examples
topics.explain: Economically important: Apis (honey bee), Bombyx (silkworm), Laccifer (lac insect). Vectors: Anopheles, Culex, Aedes (mosquitoes). Gregarious pest: Locusta. Others: Limulus, butterfly, scorpion, prawn.

topics.title: Amphibians and reptiles
topics.explain: Amphibians: two pairs of limbs, moist skin without scales, eyes with eyelids, tympanum, cloaca, external fertilisation, respiration by gills, lungs and skin. Reptiles: dry cornified skin with scales or scutes, no external ear opening, internal fertilisation, eggs with shells, snakes and lizards shed skin as cast.

topics.title: Birds
topics.explain: Feathers, beak, forelimbs modified into wings, hind limbs with scales, pneumatic bones, crop and gizzard, air sacs connected to lungs, four-chambered heart, oviparous with direct development. Flightless birds include Struthio (ostrich), Aptenodytes (penguin).

topics.title: Mammals
topics.explain: Mammary glands, hair, external pinnae, different types of teeth, four-chambered heart, mostly viviparous. Pteropus (flying fox) flies; Balaenoptera (blue whale), Delphinus (dolphin) live in water; Macropus (kangaroo) is a marsupial.

ratta: Coelom: acoelomate flatworms, pseudocoelomate roundworms, rest coelomate.
Arthropoda largest phylum;  Limulus = living fossil.
Notochord: larval tail (Uro), head to tail (Cephalo).
Platypus lays eggs;  Torpedo electric;  Trygon sting.
